It reports specific arrangements—Adani's joint venture with Jabil Inc. to build servers locally in Visakhapatnam alongside Alphabet; Ambani's 168-megawatt data center for Meta on the western coast plus a $100 million partnership selling Llama software; and Tata Group building a 100-megawatt facility for OpenAI with an option to scale to 1 gigawatt—attributed as announced plans. It notes Ambani's more than 500 million telecom subscribers, Adani's control of power infrastructure, and that large Indian groups can fund chip purchases from cash flows in refining, telecoms, ports, utilities, and software exports rather than vendor financing; these are reported claims about capacity. State Department officials Rubio reportedly met with Adani and Tata Chairman N. Chandrasekaran during a visit to India last month before touring Ambani's Jamnagar complex. The article flags uncertainties: US authorities suspect former Megaspeed International executive Alice Huang of spying for China, which the piece frames as turning Asian compute exports into a geopolitical risk; whether Pax Silica holds depends on an upcoming Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen and possible trade concessions to Beijing; foreign data centers are described as legally required to conduct deep know-your-customer audits on tenants' ownership; and Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal have questioned the Justice Department's decision to drop a bribery indictment against Gautam Adani, with Democrats expected to regain subpoena power in January. The piece concludes that retaining this position will require proving enforcement of Washington's red lines.
items.title: Nvidia's ouster positions Ambani and Adani as favored AI-infrastructure partners for US tech firms

items.summary: National Investigation Agency chief Rakesh Aggarwal rejected allegations of custodial torture made by US citizen Mathew VanDyke, stating that the accused never raised any complaint about his incarceration in Tihar jail during judicial custody. The NIA chief noted that VanDyke appeared before a Delhi court six to seven times while detained. VanDyke is accused of using India as a transit route to train insurgents in Myanmar and reportedly spent over six months in prison, which he attributed to Russia's war against Ukraine.
items.title: NIA chief rejects US citizen VanDyke's custodial torture claims

items.summary: During a visit to personnel aboard the aircraft carrier USS George Washington (CVN-73) in the Indian Ocean, US ambassador to India Sergio Gor described New Delhi as one of America's most trusted partners and said the two countries' defence partnership would define the 21st century. Speaking to crew members, he characterised India as one of the few nations Washington "truly trust[s]" and framed the relationship as strategic rather than transactional, citing access to American technology, training, military planning and senior-leadership engagement. Gor attributed priority status for the partnership to President Donald Trump and pointed to a 10-year framework for the US-India Major Defence Partnership signed in October 2025. He cited joint exercises including Tarang Shakti, Yudh Abhyas, Tiger Triumph and Malabar as evidence of expanding cooperation across land, sea and air domains; he said Tiger Triumph integrated operational cyber elements for the first time while Malabar demonstrated growing naval coordination in high-end maritime warfare. The fifth edition of Tiger Triumph ran from October 31 to November 5, 2026, with a focus on humanitarian assistance and disaster relief operations per India's ministry of defence. USNI News reported that the carrier arrived in the region on August 19 after nearly three months in the Middle East to relieve USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-71) under the 5th Fleet before returning to the 7th Fleet area of operations on November 18; it is homeported at Yokosuka, Japan. The ambassador's remarks are attributed claims about India's strategic standing and future partnership trajectory rather than established outcomes.
items.title: US ambassador Sergio Gor calls India a trusted defence partner aboard USS George Washington

items.summary: The Greater Noida Authority imposed a fine of ₹1 lakh on Antony Waste Handling Cell Limited and Yaduvanshi Infratech Private Limited, reported by Press Trust of India (PTI), for allegedly generating excessive dust during mechanical road-sweeping operations. The action followed social media complaints, including a video showing the machines producing dust clouds without spraying water first. Notices were issued on Wednesday requiring responses within three days, with blacklisting threatened if explanations proved unsatisfactory. Rajesh Kumar of the Authority's Health Department said both firms operate and maintain truck-mounted sweeping machines in Greater Noida and that officials consider the resulting dust serious negligence; roads must be sprayed before cleaning per directives from the National Green Tribunal (NGT), Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB). Penalties will be recovered by deducting amounts from future bill payments. Deputy General Manager Vijay Rawal said strict action would follow against any polluter, though these statements are claims rather than established outcomes.
items.title: Greater Noida Authority fines two road-sweeping firms ₹1 lakh each over dust pollution

items.summary: Per South Western Railway's announcement via its X handle, bulk and group reservation rules were revised through Commercial Circular (Coaching) No. 37/2026 and Rate Advice No. 11 of 2026, which replace earlier guidelines. The central change is the removal of the fixed cap on berths that can be sanctioned for group bookings; under the new rules Chief Reservation Supervisors and Station Managers may approve such reservations without a berth limit, whereas previously allotments were constrained by proportion-of-available-berth restrictions. Authorities state the facility applies to all train classes, targets genuine passengers (weddings, educational trips, pilgrimages, sporting events, cultural programmes), must not be used to block berths, and requires applicants to give each traveller's full name, age, gender, address and purpose of travel while stating their journey reason; requests at major reservation centres are accepted from 9 am on the first day of the Advance Reservation Period. The report is attributed to Livemint News Desk.
items.title: South Western Railway removes berth cap on group train bookings
